'''''Pedicularis sylvatica''''', commonly known as '''common lousewort''',<ref name=Farmer/> is a plant species in the genus ''[[Pedicularis]]''. It is native to central and northern Europe where it grows on moist acidic soils, moorland, grassy heathland and the drier parts of marshes.<ref name=Atlas>{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/pedicularis-sylvatica |title=''Pedicularis sylvatica'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish flora |access-date=28 January 2020 |archive-date=28 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128200217/https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/pedicularis-sylvatica |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Description==
This is a compact [[Biennial plant|biennial]] herb with a semi-erect stem up to {{convert|15|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} tall. The leaves are opposite, with short stalks, rather thick and often tinged pink or purple. The leaf blades are small, triangular-lanceolate to linear, with pinnate lobes and toothed margins. The inflorescence is a [[raceme]] with usually four to six flowers open at a time. Each bilaterally symmetrical flower has a large, rounded, five-angled pinkish [[Sepal|calyx]], the four lobes being tipped with teeth, which can easily be observed before the flower has opened. The flower is pinkish-purple with white markings in the throat, and up to {{convert|2.5|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} in length. The five [[petal]]s are fused into a tube, the upper lip is curved into a hood, having two teeth at the tip. The lower lip is divided into three lobes.<ref name=Farmer>{{cite web |url=http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/scrophulariaceae/pedicularis-sylvatica.htm |title=Common Lousewort: ''Pedicularis sylvatica'' |author=Farmer, Carl |work=West Highland Flora |access-date=29 January 2020 |archive-date=12 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220712101304/http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/scrophulariaceae/pedicularis-sylvatica.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://wildflowerfinder.org.uk/Flowers/L/Lousewort/Lousewort.htm|title=Lousewort: ''Pedicularis sylvatica'' |work=Wild Flowers |access-date=29 January 2020}}</ref> This species can be distinguished from [[Pedicularis palustris|marsh lousewort]] (''Pedicularis palustris'') by being smaller and less erect and having two small teeth at the tip of the upper lip rather than four.<ref name=Farmer/>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Pedicularis sylvatica Sturm54.jpg|thumb|left|Illustration from book ''Deutschlands Flora in Abbildungen'']]
Common lousewort is found in most of Europe, apart from the southeast. In the British Isles it occurs on damp acidic soils in Scotland, Ireland, Wales, northern and southwestern England, and in scattered locations elsewhere in England, at altitudes up to about {{convert|915|m|ft|-1|abbr=on}}. Typical habitats include moorland, wet flushes in mountainous areas, grassy heathland, lakesides and the drier parts of marshes and bogs.<ref name=Atlas/>

==Ecology==
The origin of the common name is that there was a belief in times past that livestock that ate this plant would acquire [[Louse|lice]] as a consequence.<ref name=NBN/> Like other members of the [[genus]], common lousewort is semi-parasitic, supplementing its own resources by connecting its roots to those of nearby plants and extracting water and nutrients for its own use.<ref name=NBN>{{cite web |url=https://species.nbnatlas.org/species/NBNSYS0000004131 |title=''Pedicularis sylvatica'' L.: Lousewort |work=NBN Atlas |access-date=29 January 2020}}</ref>
